=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: lines 12009-12019 (the `post_merge_head_sha` block in `finalize_integration_merge_if_needed`); the head-resolution at lines 11915-11920 and `pr_json` fetched at the top of the function | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The "head moved during merge attempt" detection reads `post_merge_head_sha` from the same `${pr_json}` that was fetched at the top of the function (line ~11915). When `gh pr merge --match-head-commit "${pr_head_sha}"` fails because GitHub refused (head moved), the code falls into the new block that tries to compare `post_merge_head_sha` (from stale `pr_json`) against `pr_head_sha` (also from the same stale `pr_json`). Both values are identical, so `[ "${post_merge_head_sha}" != "${pr_head_sha}" ]` is always false. The intended "retry without spending the final-merge budget" path never triggers; instead, the code falls through to the post-merge-attempt conflict/heal flow (and would spend the final-merge budget on a subsequent attempt).
  WHY: When GitHub refuses a `--match-head-commit` merge because the PR author pushed between the checks and the merge, the helper logs `ORCH_MERGE_HEAD_BOUND ... outcome=attempt` but never logs `outcome=failed reason=head_moved`. The function returns 1 via the heal path, so the next tick re-runs the merge attempt, and a sustained push loop can drain `MAX_FINAL_MERGE_ATTEMPTS` (default 3) on a head the orchestrator was supposed to defer on. The changelog claim that "a moved head on the final merge does not use up the final-merge attempt budget" is not realised.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh: line 21588 (`_orch_squash_merge_bound "${PW_PR}" "${_pw_head_sha}" auto`) and line 22285 (`_orch_squash_merge_bound "${RTM_PR}" "${_rtm_head_sha}" auto`) in the backward-scan and ready-to-merge loops | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The backward-scan and ready-to-merge loops now route through `_orch_squash_merge_bound` with `_pw_head_sha` and `_rtm_head_sha` respectively. If those locals are ever unset, empty, or non-40-hex at the call site, the helper returns 2 (no gh call) and prints `outcome=refused reason=unresolved_head_sha`, but every existing caller uses `if _orch_squash_merge_bound ... auto; then refresh_integration_backpressure_gate_after_merge || true` (or a similar success-only branch) — the refused branch silently turns into "no merge attempted, no backpressure refresh, no log line outside the helper", leaving a PR that previously would have been auto-merged via the unbound path now stranded.
  WHY: Without a verified 40-hex head SHA at these call sites, `_orch_squash_merge_bound` will refuse to call `gh` and the poller loop will not retry on its own — only the next 5-minute tick re-resolves the head SHA. For the backward-scan PRs and ready-to-merge PRs that previously merged fine without head binding, this turns a working merge path into a silent regression when the earlier head-resolution read returned empty (e.g., API pagination, malformed response). The test `test_every_poller_merge_is_head_bound` only checks that the literal call site exists; it does not verify that `_pw_head_sha` / `_rtm_head_sha` are populated before use.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
